message.content:
Sure! If you’ve already started `timer.exe` (or left an instance running) and now want to stop it **and** clean up the executable from your machine, here’s what you’ll do:

---

### 1️⃣ Kill the Running Process  
Open Command Prompt **as Administrator** and type:

```cmd
taskkill /IM timer.exe /F
```

* `/IM timer.exe` – tells Task Kill which image name to target.  
* `/F` – forces termination even if the program tries to stay alive.

If you’re sure there isn’t another legitimate “timer” app on this PC, this will close all instances instantly.

> ⚠️ *Tip:* You can also list currently running processes first:
>
> ```cmd
> tasklist | findstr /i timer.exe
> ```

---

### 2️⃣ Delete the Executable File  

Once no instance is running, locate where the file lives. Common places include:

| Typical Location | Example Path |
|------------------|--------------|
| Program Files    | `C:\Program Files\timer.exe` |
| AppData          | `%APPDATA%\TimerApp\timer.exe` |
| Desktop/Downloads| `C:\Users\<you>\Desktop\timer.exe` |

Navigate to that folder in Explorer or use CMD:

```cmd
del "C:\Path\To\timer.exe"
```

Replace `"C:\Path\To\timer.exe"` with the actual full path.  
If the file is protected or locked, make sure you ran CMD as Admin.

---

#### Quick One‑liner (if you know the exact path)

```cmd
taskkill /IM timer.exe /F && del "C:\Full\Path\to\timer.exe"
```

This kills the process **then deletes** the file—only works when both steps succeed.

---

### 3️⃣ Verify Removal

Run again:

```cmd
where timer.exe
```

It should return nothing (`INFO: Could Not Find...`). Or check the directory manually.

---

That’s it! Your `timer.exe` has been stopped and removed. Let me know if you hit any snags or need help locating the file.
